topic: Smoker walked away from his Loguetown post to chase Luffy, and the chase kept going
title: Smoker Abandoned His Post For One Pirate
description: Smoker was supposed to guard Loguetown, and instead he sailed after Luffy with his subordinate Tashigi. Here's the detail that makes his chase look personal. Do you think it was duty or something else?
comment: Duty or grudge: why did Smoker chase Luffy across the Grand Line? Pick one.

lines.text: Smoker abandoned his post in Loguetown to chase one pirate.

shot.fallback: stern Marine captain on a harbor dock

lines.text: A fellow Marine reminded him of his duties.

shot.fallback: Marine soldier on a harbor pier

lines.text: Smoker's reply? They could not order him around.

shot.fallback: Marine captain with a sharp glare

lines.text: Then he sailed for the Grand Line with Tashigi.

shot.fallback: Marine warship sailing on open sea

lines.text: That's not a Marine following orders. That's a Marine following Luffy.

shot.fallback: Marine captain staring at a pirate

lines.text: Look at Alabasta. He and Tashigi captured Mr. 11.

shot.fallback: Marine officers capturing a masked man

lines.text: Then he intercepted a call between Mr. 0 and Sanji.

shot.fallback: black snail phone on a desk

lines.text: One name stood out to him: Princess Vivi.
Then he handed off his forces and left on a private mission.

shot.fallback: Marine captain passing command to his subordinate

lines.text: The Navy credited him with beating Crocodile.

shot.fallback: Marine officer beside a desert battlefield

lines.text: He refused that promotion, then accepted it anyway.

shot.fallback: Marine officer receiving a new rank

lines.text: Why? A higher rank meant more freedom to chase Luffy.

shot.fallback: Marine captain looking toward the sea
Marine captain staring down a pirate

lines.text: Because a Marine who abandons his post for one pirate has already picked his answer.

self_check.hook: Names Smoker and his abandoned post in the first two seconds.
self_check.loop: Last line says a Marine who abandons his post for one pirate has already picked his answer, which leads back into line 1.
